idea: Safety #1 – hot things (LIVING ROOM): soft white steam puffs up from Baby Ava's pink mug of warm milk right as she reaches for it ('Oh! Look, steam! It's hot, hot, hot!'); she pulls her hands back and puts them on her tummy, shaking her head ('Hot, hot! Don't touch! Hands on your tummy!' – copy-me); Mommy Lily kneels beside her and holds up one finger ('Mommy, is it hot? Wait, wait, wait!'); Ava blows on the milk ('Blow with me! Whoo, whoo, whoo!' – copy-me) until the steam is gone; she asks the viewer 'Is it hot? Do we touch? Hmm?' (pause) – 'No, no! We wait and blow!'; lesson 'Hot? Don't touch! Ask a grown-up!'. Loop: the hook framing again, now no steam, hand on her cooled mug, bye-bye wave.
title: Oh! It's Hot! ☕ Hot Hot, Don't Touch! Safety Song with Baby Ava | Crayon Babies
description:
Oh! Look, steam! Baby Ava's warm milk is too hot – so she doesn't touch it! ☕ Sing along as Ava puts her hands on her tummy, waits with Mommy Lily and blows – whoo, whoo – until her milk is nice and warm.

🎬 What happens in this video:
😮 "Oh! Look, steam! It's hot, hot, hot!"
✋ Hot, hot! Don't touch! Hands on your tummy!
👩 Mommy Lily says: wait, wait, wait!
🌬️ Blow with Ava: whoo, whoo, whoo!
🤔 "Is it hot? Do we touch?" – can you answer?
👋 Hot? Don't touch! Ask a grown-up! Bye bye, friends!

📚 Kids learn: safety with hot things • hot • don't touch • wait • blow • ask a grown-up

A fun sing-along cartoon for toddlers and preschoolers about staying safe around hot food and drinks, with Baby Ava and Mommy Lily in the Crayon House living room.
